rv.q: It’s messy, fascinating, and heedless of the rules —and isn’t it nice that an Academy Award-winning Yale professor of playwrighting can still write something like that?
Ms. Blakk for President certainly has my vote, but I wish I could cast it with more enthusiasm.
The “purposes of the play” seem less a profile of a person or a historic accounting than a lively entertainment, albeit one punctuated with a polemic.
But Ms. Blakk for President is sprawling at the expense of creating a truly rich and focused study of character, time, place, and politics.
Tony winner Ato Blankson-Wood ( Slave Play ) turns in a virtuoso performance as Smith/Blakk.
That said, for the engaged audience member, it’s absolutely dazzling.
While fun and entertaining, doesn't reach deep enough to uproot or unsettle.
Ms. Blakk for President remains a musical in search of its own identity.
As a time-warp drag show with plenty of surface glitz, Ms. Blakk for President can be a lot of fun.

cn.t: Critics find this vibrant account of drag queen Joan Jett Blakk's 1992 presidential run visually striking and well-performed by Ato Blankson-Wood, though some feel it prioritizes entertainment over deeper examination of its activist subject.
